suggestions.rationale: Clinical Mapping Master Resolution 2026 publishes this relationship only as disease complication with chronicity guard. Require documented multiple myeloma and separately documented chronic kidney disease satisfying accepted chronicity criteria. Where the relationship is represented as myeloma-related CKD, require clinical evidence linking the renal disease to myeloma-associated pathology, such as light-chain/cast nephropathy, monoclonal-protein-associated renal disease, or other appropriately established myeloma-related renal injury. Do not relabel transient AKI, an isolated creatinine elevation, or nonspecific renal impairment as CKD, and do not assume all CKD in a patient with multiple myeloma is caused by the myeloma. The cited literature supports only this bounded proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-5 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Require documented multiple myeloma and separately established anemia. The source supports anemia as a common myeloma manifestation but does not establish that every anemia in a patient with myeloma is attributable to the malignancy. Preserve chronic kidney disease, blood loss, nutritional deficiency, hemolysis, treatment-related marrow suppression, other marrow disorders, and other anemia etiologies as competing or contributing explanations. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
